question: Match the device: 50, 51, and 87.
choices: 50 time overcurrent, 51 instantaneous, 87 lockout
50 instantaneous overcurrent, 51 time overcurrent, 87 differential
50 differential, 51 distance, 87 frequency
50 undervoltage, 51 overvoltage, 87 reclosing
explanation: 50 is instantaneous overcurrent, 51 is time overcurrent, 87 is differential. 86 is the lockout. 27 and 59 are the voltage elements. Learn the numbers; the one-line will not spell them out.
reference: IEEE C37.2 device numbers, as used in ATS 7.9.1 element tests

question: ATS 7.9.1 tells you to determine which of the following on an 87 differential?
choices: Only the target color
Operating-unit pickup, restraint, slope, and harmonic restraint
The transformer's oil interfacial tension
A 10-minute polarization index of the relay case only
explanation: The 87 list is operating-unit pickup, each restraint unit, slope, harmonic restraint, instantaneous pickup, and the plotted restraint characteristic. The paragraph says to determine harmonic restraint; it does not name the second harmonic in that sentence.

question: Functional checks in ATS 7.9.1 include proving that relay contacts perform which scheme jobs?
choices: Breaker trip, close inhibit, 86 lockout, and alarms
Only the front-panel lamp test
Oil sampling and a turns-ratio test
A Wenner soil box on the station ground
explanation: The functional paragraph names breaker trip tests, close inhibit, 86 lockout tests, and alarm functions, and points at Section 8. A relay that asserts in the test set but never moves the trip wire is not finished.

question: A CT primary is carrying load and someone opens the secondary at the terminal block. The hazard is:
choices: The secondary voltage collapses to zero and is safe to hold
The secondary can develop a dangerous voltage while it tries to maintain ampere-turns
Only the revenue meter is affected; the leads stay at a few volts
The CT automatically shorts itself inside the head
explanation: An open CT secondary with primary current flowing can rise to a hazardous voltage. Short the secondary or leave it on its burden before the primary is energized. ATS also requires exactly one secondary ground, at the place the drawings show.
reference: CT secondary practice; ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.10.1.B.9 (one grounding point). Open-circuit voltage is standard CT behavior.

question: You need to see whether an 86 contact is in the breaker close circuit. Which drawing actually shows the coil and the contact?
choices: The one-line, because it shows every contact
The control schematic (or elementary), not the one-line
The site plot plan
The oil lab report
explanation: A one-line shows the power path and the device numbers. The control schematic shows coils, a and b contacts, and how a lockout is inserted into trip and close. Asking a one-line to carry the close-permissive contact is the print trap.
reference: Drawing practice; ATS 7.9.1 functional tests still require the contact to perform its scheme job

question: ATS 7.22.1 for an engine generator tells you to verify, as the application requires:
choices: Only the fuel-filter color
Phase rotation, phasing, and synchronized operation
That synchronization is optional if the breaker is closed fast
Winding resistance instead of rotation
explanation: 7.22.1.B.3 and the matching test-value line require phase rotation, phasing, and synchronizing to match the system design. Closing a generator onto a live bus with the wrong rotation is a fault, not a commissioning footnote.

question: A 51 contact energizes an 86 lockout, and an 86 contact energizes the breaker trip coil. In that path, what operates first?
choices: The 86 coil
The 52 trip coil
The 51 element
The breaker springs, before any relay
explanation: The 51 has to pick up and close its contact before the 86 coil is energized. The 86 then seals and its contact energizes the trip coil, so the breaker opens third in this particular path. Resetting the breaker does not reset the 86.
reference: Control-schematic sequence; ATS 7.9.1 includes 51 pickup and 86 lockout functional tests

question: An 86 b contact is in the close-permissive string. The lockout trips (coil picked up). That b contact:
choices: Closes and allows a close
Opens and blocks closing until the lockout is reset
Does not change, because b contacts are not used in trip circuits
Becomes an a contact automatically
explanation: A b contact is closed when the device is de-energized and open when the device is picked up. A tripped 86 opens its b contact and removes close permission. An a contact would do the opposite and is the one you would use to energize a trip or an alarm when the lockout operates.
